chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Surely God is too Majestic and Generous to be known through His creation; rather, creation is known through God.' He said: 'You speak the truth.' I said: 'Surely one who recognizes that he has a Lord, it is befitting for him to recognize that that Lord has pleasure and wrath, and that His pleasure and wrath cannot be known except through revelation or a messenger. So whoever does not receive revelation, it is befitting for him to seek the messengers. When he meets them, he should recognize that they are the Divine Authority (hujja) and that obedience to them is obligatory.'

So I said to the people: 'Do you not know that the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) was the Divine Authority from God over His creation?' They said: 'Yes.' I said: 'So when he passed away, who was the Divine Authority?' They said: 'The Quran.' So I looked into the Quran and found that the Murji'ites, the Qadariyya, and the atheist who does not believe in it, all use it in debate to the point of defeating men in their argumentation. So I recognized that the Quran cannot be a Divine Authority except with a custodian (qayyim), and whatever he says about it is the truth.

So I said to them: 'Who is the custodian of the Quran?' They said: 'Ibn Mas'ud knew parts of it, and Umar knew, and Hudhayfa knew.' I said: 'All of it?' They said: 'No.' So I could not find anyone who could be said to know the Quran in its entirety except Ali (may God's blessings be upon him); and whenever there was a matter among the people, this one said: 'I do not know', that one said: 'I do not know', another said: 'I do not know', while he said: 'I do know.'

Thus I testify that Ali (peace be upon him) was the custodian of the Quran, that obedience to him was obligatory, and that he was the Divine Authority over the people after the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), and that whatever he said about the Quran is the truth.' So he (the Imam) said: 'May God have mercy on you!' So I said: 'Surely Ali (peace be upon him) did not depart until he left a Divine Authority after him, just as the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) had left; and the Divine Authority after Ali was al-Hasan ibn Ali.' And I testify about al-Hasan that he did not depart until he left a Divine Authority after him, just as his father and grandfather had left; and the Divine Authority after al-Hasan was al-Husayn, and obedience to him was obligatory.' So he said: 'May God have mercy on you!'

So I kissed his head and said: 'And I testify about al-Husayn (peace be upon him) that he did not depart until he left a Divine Authority after him: Ali ibn al-Husayn, and obedience to him was obligatory.' So he said: 'May God have mercy on you!' So I kissed his head and said: 'And I testify about Ali ibn al-Husayn that he did not depart until he left a Divine Authority after him: Muhammad ibn Ali, Abu Ja'far, and obedience to him was obligatory.' So he said: 'May God have mercy on you!'

I said: 'Give me your head so I may kiss it.' So he laughed. I said: 'May God keep you well! I know full well that your father did not depart until he left a Divine Authority after him, just as his father had left; and I testify by God that you are the Divine Authority and that obedience to you is obligatory.' So he said: 'Stop — may God have mercy on you!' I said: 'Give me your head so I may kiss it.' So I kissed his head, and he laughed and said: 'Ask me about whatever you wish, for I will not deny you an answer after today, ever.'

key_terms.الحجة: Divine Authority / Proof of God — the infallible guide appointed by God to lead humanity
key_terms.الزنديق: Atheist/heretic — one who does not believe in the divine origin of the Quran
key_terms.الطاعة المفترضة: Obligatory obedience — the Imam's authority as a religious duty
key_terms.القدري: Qadarite — one who holds a particular view on free will and divine decree
key_terms.المرجئ: Murji'ite — one who defers judgment on faith and action
key_terms.قيم القرآن: Custodian of the Quran — the authoritative interpreter with complete knowledge of the scripture

ai.seo_question: Why is an Imam necessary as the custodian of the Quran according to Shia theology?
ai.summary: This hadith presents the famous theological argument of Mansur ibn Hazim, a companion of Imam al-Sadiq (AS), for the necessity of an Imam as the authoritative custodian of the Quran. Mansur first establishes that God's pleasure and wrath can only be known through revelation or a messenger, and then demonstrates through dialogue that the Quran alone cannot serve as a divine authority without a living, infallible interpreter. He then systematically testifies to the imamate of each Imam from Ali to Muhammad al-Baqir, and finally directly identifies Imam al-Sadiq as the current Divine Authority — to which the Imam responds with laughter and permission to ask anything.
